note: Adapted from the original description (in English) when Coaton (1955) described the species, from a single female alate, the species being new in that paper; soldier and worker unknown. Coaton notes that this alate differs in several respects from the alate of N. aburiensis described by Grassé (1937) and therefore establishes a new species.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head dark brown, far darker than and contrasting with the rest of the body. Compound eyes black, ocelli white. Anteclypeus white, labrum golden yellow, antennae brownish yellow. Pronotum brownish yellow. Meso- and metanota creamy yellow in front, becoming brownish yellow behind, each with a black median line that fades about three quarters of the way from the anterior to the posterior margin. Tergites yellowish brown, sternites a paler brownish yellow. Femora yellow, tibiae dark brown, the apical tibial spurs darker still; tarsi paler than the tibiae, the tips of the tarsal claws dark brown. Wing membrane tinged pale brown; all veins from the costa to the media dark brown, the cubitus colourless. Head and body sparsely covered with stiff bristles. Cranial, transverse and frontoclypeal sutures distinct. In dorsal view the head is semicircular behind the compound eyes. Ocelli almost oval, touching the upper margin of the compound eyes, long diameter 0.27; compound eyes well developed, distinctly projecting beyond the head outline in dorsal view, nearly circular in outline but with a straight anterior margin, long diameter 0.62. Postclypeus short and broad. Anteclypeus with straight sides converging towards the tip, the anterolateral angles obtuse and rounded into the straight anterior margin. Labrum with diverging sides, rounded into a three-faceted anterior margin. Antennae 18-segmented; segment 1 longer than segment 2, segment 3 almost club-shaped and distinctly longer than segments 2 and 4. Pronotum kidney-shaped, transversely arched, wider than the head including the compound eyes (2.10 as against 1.95); length along the midline slightly more than half the width (1.17 as against 2.10); anterior margin concave, anterolateral angles broadly rounded, sides slightly convex and two-faceted, posterolateral angles obtuse and broadly rounded into the straight posterior margin. Posterior margin of the mesonotum nearly straight, that of the metanotum shallowly but distinctly concave in the middle. Wing membrane reticulate; all veins from the costa to the media developed and sclerotized, the cubitus weak and reduced except at the base; media close against the radius sector and parallel to it, the two joined by a few short cross-veins. Fore wing veins arising independently at the wing suture; subcosta short and simple; radius unbranched, merging into the costa in the proximal half of the wing; radius sector with 7 or 8 simple or forked branches running to the costal margin; media simple, running to the tip of the wing; cubitus with a variable number of simple or forked branches running to the inner margin, distinct near the wing suture and reduced in the distal half of the wing. Hind wing radius and cubitus arising independently at the wing suture, the radius sector and media with a common stalk up to the proximal third of the wing; no subcosta; radius long, merging into the costa in the distal half of the wing, simple or with 1 branch running to the costal margin; radius sector with 7—9 simple or forked branches running to the costal margin; media simple, running to the tip of the wing; cubitus with many simple or forked branches running to the inner margin, the proximal ones distinct to about two thirds of the way distally. Fore, middle and hind tibiae each with 3 apical spurs. Cerci short, no styli; arolium present.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: A single female alate: body length (with the wings folded) 21.1 mm, without the wings 11.8 mm, wing expanse 35.4 mm, fore wing length to the wing suture 15.5—15.7 mm and width 4.62—4.66 mm, head width including the compound eyes 1.95 mm, compound eye diameter 0.62 mm, pronotum length along the midline 1.17 mm and width 2.10 mm. The measurements compared with those of N. aburiensis and N. gestri are given in Table 2: collarti is distinctly larger than aburiensis (the latter with a fore wing of 11.75 mm, body length with wings 14.5 mm, without wings 8.75 mm, head width 1.6—1.65 mm). The specimen was collected by Collart in the Kawa forest (Lake Albert), Democratic Republic of the Congo, and is held in the Tervuren museum. The type locality is in the same collecting area as that of aburiensis.
